units.translation: Three introductory trimeters by the chorus leader (1 and 3 pure iambs, in any case also recited at a rapid tempo); then three strophic pairs, in which there was undoubtedly solo delivery or divided delivery of the individual pieces; but how, is quite impossible to determine. G. Hermann distributed among 15 choreuts (including the 3 trimeters at the beginning), dividing Str. ⟦1⟧ Ant. ⟦2⟧ fivefold, among four each, Str. ⟦3⟧ Ant. ⟦4⟧ twofold among two each, Str. ⟦5⟧ Ant. ⟦6⟧ but undivided, giving one Erinys each. Rossbach, Kirchhoff, Wecklein distribute among half-choruses; with them too the splitting of Str. Ant. ⟦7⟧ is fourfold, of Str. Ant. ⟦8⟧ only single; Str. Ant. ⟦9⟧ remain units and are even given by Rossbach to the whole chorus. The scholiast notes only: ⟦10⟧ (as a detached piece, not part of a period) ⟦11⟧ · ⟦12⟧ (interruptions of the construction) ⟦13⟧; so no division was transmitted to him either. One must imagine that the Erinyes, waking one after another, sprang up, looked around, ran back and forth, but finally forward, i.e. down from the ekkyklema into the orchestra, where it was possible to group themselves and perform regular movements; therefore for Str. Ant. a the division into half-choruses seems to me excluded, for ⟦14⟧ (⟦15⟧) on the other hand permissible. According to the poet's fiction (179) they are nevertheless still inside the temple. That the excitement is strongest at first, then subsides somewhat, is natural. Of rhythms the dochmiacs dominate, to which, however, as elsewhere, recited trimeters are mixed, ⟦16⟧ 2. 4, ⟦17⟧ 1, ⟦18⟧ 1, with not many spondees, finally however (Ant. ⟦19⟧) even with three. Cf. on these trimeters at ⟦20⟧; in the second parodos and in the strophe 778 ff. the same mixture occurs. The dochmiacs correspond exactly except at 157, 164, where one emends, and 143, 149. Besides: Str. ⟦21⟧ 6~-~--~- - ~ -, cf. ⟦22⟧5 (ICICI-CIICI, but probably iambs with suppressed resolutions (⟦23⟧); on the other hand resolved iambs ⟦24⟧, 6000 / U U U / ~ ~ ~ / ~-; dochmiac and iambic dipody (cf. at ⟦25⟧, p. 86) ⟦26⟧, 2 and in reversed position (CI, CIICI) ⟦27⟧ 4; dochmiac and ⟦28⟧ ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔⟦29⟧, 2 (cf. strophe endings like 793 ⟦30⟧. 701). Very unclear is Str. ⟦31⟧: ⟦32⟧, ⟦33⟧ — ⟦34⟧, ⟦35⟧, paeons without synapheia? catalectic trochaic dipodies likewise? Cf. 328 etc. Or iambic tripody? Then the anaphora would be somewhat blurred.
